articles.title: New York Office Tenant Improvement Totals Rise in 2026 Amid Market Shifts
articles.narrative: Tenant improvement (TI) allowances in Manhattan's office market have seen a significant increase since 2019, rising 59.2 percent, with a 7.9 percent year-over-year increase to $120.80 per square foot in September 2026, according to Avison Young data. This trend, driven by landlords' need to deliver competitive spaces to attract corporate tenants making long-term commitments at high rents, diverges from the typical pattern where high interest rates would favor free rent concessions over capital-intensive TIs. The increase is particularly pronounced in trophy office assets, where TI allowances rose 15.8 percent to $130.40 per square foot, while Class B and C buildings saw a 4.3 percent decline to $103.40 per square foot, reflecting a K-shaped recovery in the market.

Lower Manhattan has been slower to recover from post-pandemic vacancies, though residential conversions have tightened supply by removing weaker buildings.

articles.title: StageLynk Launches AI Booking Platform for Film and TV Stages
articles.narrative: StageLynk, a Los Angeles-based startup with an office in Chicago, has launched an AI-powered platform designed to streamline the booking and production planning process for film and television soundstages. The platform, which includes an AI production assistant called StageScout, connects studio owners with production companies by offering a searchable directory of nearly 17 million square feet across 1,200 soundstages in major production hubs. It helps production teams evaluate factors beyond just the stage, such as tax incentives, permitting, union considerations, and local amenities, while also serving as a marketing and lead-generation tool for studios to manage bookings and increase visibility in a competitive market.

articles.title: Kayla Lee of Serhant: 5 Questions
articles.narrative: This article features an interview with Kayla Lee, a prominent broker at Serhant, who discusses her decade-long career in real estate, during which she has sold over $1 billion across more than 850 units. Lee specializes in new development projects, particularly in Brooklyn and Queens, where she leverages her hyper-local expertise. She highlights the appeal of the outer boroughs for new development due to their convenience to Manhattan, vibrant communities, and access to green spaces. Lee also notes evolving buyer preferences, with a growing demand for natural light, higher ceilings, better views, and intelligent design features in residential projects, reflecting a shift towards more time spent at home.

articles.title: NYC’s Development Site Market Is Changing. So Is the Way We Create Value.
articles.narrative: The New York City development site market is experiencing a significant resurgence, with anticipated sales volume increasing over 30 percent this year compared to 2025. This growth is driven by expanding buyer demand, intensifying competition for well-positioned sites, and increasing opportunities to create value through zoning changes. The article highlights that the Department of City Planning's receptiveness to rezonings is a key factor, leading some brokers to advise owners to pursue rezoning before selling to maximize value, despite the inherent risks. The market is also seeing an expanding universe of purchasers for smaller Manhattan sites, including established developers from other boroughs, which further intensifies competition and expands the pool of potential buyers.

articles.title: How Bad Would an AI Bust Be for New York’s Office Market?
articles.narrative: New York City Comptroller Mark Levine's May 2026 report, "AI and New York City’s Fiscal Future: Planning Scenarios for an Uncertain Economy," highlights the city's significant exposure to both the opportunities and risks of artificial intelligence, particularly given its reliance on the financial industry. The report outlines five potential scenarios for AI's economic impact, with varying probabilities, including a 35% chance of productivity boosts with limited disruption and a 25% chance of AI investment fizzling. Despite these economic uncertainties and broader concerns about AI's societal impact, Manhattan's office market has seen a substantial increase in AI-related leasing, with AI companies accounting for 8.2% of new leasing in the first half of 2026, up from 0.7% in 2020. This growth includes a shift from subleasing to direct deals and a significant increase in average lease terms. While the overall percentage of Manhattan office space occupied by AI companies remains relatively small at around 1%, industry experts like Gabe Marans of Savills and Jeff Gural of GFP Real Estate acknowledge the growing importance of AI tenants, particularly for Class B office owners, suggesting that while a potential AI bust might not cripple the entire market, it could have outsized effects on properties with a high concentration of AI tenants.

articles.title: Colliers Brokers Sale of Two-Property Self-Storage Portfolio in Wisconsin
articles.narrative: Colliers has facilitated the sale of a two-property self-storage portfolio in Wisconsin, totaling 171,825 square feet and 1,486 units. Inland Real Estate acquired the portfolio from Bruno Self Storage LLC. The properties, located in Pleasant Prairie and West Bend, are managed by Extra Space and were completed in 2020 and 2019, respectively.

data_points.project_notes: The Pleasant Prairie facility was completed in 2020, and the West Bend facility was completed in 2019.

articles.title: PCCP Provides $41M Refinancing for Multifamily Community in San Diego
articles.narrative: PCCP has provided a $41 million senior loan to Foulger-Pratt for the refinancing of Tenney North Park, a 125-unit multifamily community in San Diego's North Park submarket. The loan refinances an existing construction loan for the recently built property, which features a mix of market-rate and affordable units, ground-floor retail, and a comprehensive amenity package.

data_points.address: 2260 El Cajon Blvd, San Diego, CA

The asset includes a two-story parking structure with over 600 stalls. The terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

articles.title: DAUM Negotiates $10.6M Sale of Industrial Building in Phoenix
articles.narrative: DAUM Commercial Real Estate Services has facilitated the $10.6 million sale of a 43,338-square-foot industrial building in Phoenix's Deer Valley submarket. A private Taiwanese investment company acquired the asset from a privately held California company in an off-market transaction. The property features single-tenant industrial space with 6,500 square feet of office, fully air-conditioned office and manufacturing areas, 18-foot clear heights, and multiple loading doors.

articles.narrative: Brown Commercial Group recently brokered a 45,196-square-foot industrial lease for Clarke Packing & Crating at Blue Heron 160 in Bartlett, Illinois. The specialized packaging company will relocate its operations and approximately 40 employees to the modern facility, seeking improved operational efficiencies and a central location near Chicago's transportation corridors. Blue Heron 160 was developed to meet demand from small to mid-sized industrial tenants, offering state-of-the-art features like 32-foot clear heights and ample truck docks.

articles.title: Hiffman National surpasses 100 million square feet of CRE under management
articles.narrative: Hiffman National has surpassed 100 million square feet of commercial real estate under management, reaching over 104 million square feet across 665 properties nationwide as of September 2026. This milestone reflects significant organic growth driven by existing clients expanding into new markets, allowing the firm to extend its hands-on management approach across various property types including office, medical office, industrial, and retail. The firm's expansion includes new assignments in Arizona and a 167,000-square-foot office property in downtown Chicago, demonstrating its ability to grow alongside its client base while maintaining service quality.

articles.title: Location, Timing, Connection Drove World Cup Gains in Host Cities
articles.narrative: A new white paper by Placer.ai and Colliers analyzes the economic impact of the 2026 FIFA World Cup on its 11 U.S. host cities, revealing that while the tournament provided a substantial boost, the benefits were highly localized. Metro-wide retail and dining sectors saw only marginal to modest lifts; instead, the most significant gains accrued to businesses and properties strategically located near stadiums and fan zones. The report emphasizes that successful economic leverage from major events hinges on precise location, opportune timing, and a direct connection to the event's fan journey, with well-placed fan destinations capable of extending the economic footprint beyond immediate venues.

articles.title: Urban Outfitters–Leased Retail Condo in Wicker Park Changes Hands
articles.narrative: Greenstone Partners has facilitated the sale of a 10,600-square-foot retail condominium in Chicago's Wicker Park neighborhood for $4.125 million. The property, fully leased to a national apparel retailer, was sold by Newcastle Investors. The retailer has been a long-standing presence in the area, having occupied the space since 2005.

data_points.notable_features: Two-level retail condominium with an additional 2,676-square-foot lower level and approximately 50 feet of frontage on Milwaukee Avenue.
data_points.project_notes: The seller, Newcastle Investors, acquired the property in 2013. The tenant has occupied the property since 2005.

articles.title: Sterling Bay Achieves Full Retail Occupancy at 123 N. Wacker
articles.narrative: Sterling Bay has achieved full retail occupancy at its 123 N. Wacker Drive property in Chicago's central business district. The firm, which has managed leasing, property, and asset management for the building since 2024, has successfully curated a mix of retail and office tenants, demonstrating the value of strategic tenant curation in attracting occupants and driving long-term value.

data_points.project_notes: Sterling Bay has served as leasing, property, and asset management for the building since 2024.

articles.title: Amazon Leases 91K-SF Warehouse in Everett
articles.narrative: Amazon has signed a new lease for a 90,970-square-foot warehouse in Everett, WA, to support its Leo satellite division. This marks Amazon's return to a facility it previously occupied, which had been vacant since 2022. The property's proximity to Amazon's existing 167,000-square-foot logistics hub for its orbital satellite division makes it a strategic location for the company's expanding low Earth orbit satellite broadband network.

data_points.notable_features: Located near Amazon's 167,000-square-foot logistics hub for its orbital satellite division.
data_points.project_notes: Amazon previously occupied this facility from 2018 until 2024.

The property, situated in the North Shore trade area across from the Bayshore mixed-use development, was acquired by SW Neighborhood Centers IV, an affiliate of Shannon Waltchack, from a private investor. The transaction generated multiple competitive offers and closed with an all-cash institutional buyer within 45 days.

articles.title: Nonprofit Buys FIU Student Housing Building For $169M: The South Florida Deal Sheet
articles.narrative: A nonprofit organization has acquired a student housing building serving Florida International University for $169 million. This transaction positions the university for potential future ownership of the asset, indicating a strategic long-term plan for the property.

articles.title: Despite Foreclosure Litigation, Kaufman Astoria Studios Is Bouncing Back
articles.narrative: Kaufman Astoria Studios, a historic film and television production campus, has achieved 100% occupancy, signaling a strong rebound after facing challenges from the pandemic and industry strikes. This full occupancy comes despite ongoing foreclosure litigation, highlighting the studio's resilience and continued demand for its production facilities.

data_points.project_notes: Struggled through years of difficulties stemming from the pandemic and industry strikes.

articles.title: Copper Mill Sues Partners Over Collapsed Deal For 750-Unit Dorchester Project
articles.narrative: Copper Mill has filed a lawsuit against POB and Pactolus, alleging fraud in connection with a collapsed deal for a 750-unit residential project in Dorchester. The lawsuit claims that the defendants engaged in fraudulent activities related to their agreement for the development site.

articles.title: Big Banks Take Bigger CRE Losses As They Clear Out Problem Loans
articles.narrative: Major banks are actively working to reduce their exposure to troubled commercial real estate loans across various property sectors. This strategic effort is leading to a decline in both nonaccrual and nonperforming loan balances, indicating a concerted push to clear out problematic assets from their balance sheets.

articles.title: Dean Adler Looks To Sell 'The Best Property We Own'
articles.narrative: Lubert-Adler Partners has engaged CBRE to market 2400 Market St. for sale, a trophy office property in Philadelphia. The building is currently occupied by a strong mix of tenants, including a prominent club, a major financial institution, and a global food service company. Dean Adler, co-founder of Lubert-Adler, indicated that this asset represents the firm's highest quality holding.
